newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes down against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes down against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed down at 8.2960 on Monday from 8.2955 last Friday against the U.S. dollar on the foreign exchange market in Shanghai, dealers said.
They said more selling emerged on Monday after the yuan failed to rebound last Friday because investors expected the Chinese currency to fall further in the short term.
The weighted average price last Friday was 8.2954.
The yuan opened unchanged at 8.2955, hitting an intraday high of 8.2953 in early trading. It fell further to move around the 8.2960 level for most of the session, hitting a low of 8.2965.
Trading was not active, dealers said.

"More selling emerged at the 8.2950 level, which pushed the local currency down," said one dealer. "Pro-yuan sentiment has slowly changed since the central bank was seen depressing the yuan last week."
Dealers said they expected the yuan to fall further in the near future, possibly to new lows for the month.
The yuan closed little changed at 6.8800 from 6.8888 against 100 Japanese yen and up at 1.0707 from 1.0719 against the Hong Kong dollar.
